questions.text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 30 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 hours. Pipes A and B are opened together for the first 5 hours, and then Pipe C is also opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution: Shortcut (LCM Method): Take tank capacity = LCM(20, 30, 15) = 60 units. Efficiency: A = +3 units/hr, B = +2 units/hr, C = -4 units/hr. Work done by A+B in first 5 hrs = (3+2) × 5 = 25 units. Remaining = 35 units. Combined efficiency of A+B+C = 3+2-4 = +1 unit/hr. Time for remaining = 35 / 1 = 35 hrs. Total time = 5 + 35 = 40 hrs. Step-by-step: 1) Let capacity = 60 units (LCM). 2) A's rate = 3 u/hr, B's rate = 2 u/hr, C's rate = -4 u/hr. 3) First 5 hours: (3+2) × 5 = 25 units filled. 4) Remaining capacity = 60 - 25 = 35 units. 5) Net rate with all three open = 3 + 2 - 4 = 1 u/hr. 6) Time to fill remaining = 35 / 1 = 35 hours. 7) Total time = 5 + 35 = 40 hours.

questions.text: In the following sentence, four words are highlighted as (A), (B), (C), and (D). One pair of words needs to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct. Identify the correct pair. The **decision** (A) to **implement** (B) the new policy was **review** (C) after a thorough **taken** (D) of the feedback.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check Part of Speech fit. 'Was ______' needs a Past Participle (V3). 'Taken' (V3) fits after 'was'. 'A thorough ______' needs a Noun. 'Review' (Noun) fits. Swap C (Verb) and D (V3/Noun) to get 'was taken' and 'thorough review'. Full Solution: The structure 'was review' is incorrect (passive voice requires V3 'taken'). The structure 'thorough taken' is incorrect (adjective 'thorough' modifies a noun 'review'). Swapping 'review' (C) and 'taken' (D) yields 'was taken' (correct passive) and 'thorough review' (correct noun phrase).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate pair of words to fill in the blanks. The manager's ______ attitude towards the recurring complaints only served to ______ the frustration of the employees.
questions.solution: Shortcut: The phrase 'only served to' signals a negative consequence. The first blank needs a negative adjective ('indifferent'), and the second blank needs a verb meaning 'worsen' ('exacerbate'). Eliminate positive pairs (proactive/mitigate). Full Solution: 'Indifferent' means showing no interest/concern (negative). 'Exacerbate' means to make worse. 'Mitigate' means to reduce (positive). 'Proactive' is positive. A negative cause (indifferent) leads to a negative effect (exacerbate).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The peace talks between the two nations have been put **on the back burner** due to the ongoing border tensions.
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Back burner' refers to the rear stove burners where pots simmer unattended. It metaphorically means low priority/postponement. Eliminate extremes like 'cancelled' or 'top priority'. Full Solution: The idiom 'on the back burner' means to postpone a task or give it lower priority while focusing on something else. The context of 'ongoing border tensions' forcing talks to wait confirms this meaning.

questions.text: Five friends – G, H, I, J, and K – are standing in a line facing north. G is somewhere to the left of H. I stands exactly two places to the right of G. J is not at an end. K stands immediately to the right of H. Who is standing at the far right end?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Place K immediately right of H, so H cannot be at far right. Since J is not at an end, the ends must be G or I or K. I is two places right of G, so G cannot be at far right. Thus K must be at far right. Full reasoning: Try positions 1‑5. Let H be at position x, then K at x+1. G left of H, so G ≤ x‑1. I = G+2. Test possibilities; only arrangement G‑I‑H‑K‑J satisfies all, putting K at position 5 (far right).

questions.text: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct. Having finished the assignment, the television was turned on by him.

options.label: A
options.text: Having finished the assignment, the television was turned on by him

options.label: B
options.text: After finishing the assignment, the television was turned on by him

options.label: C
options.text: Having finished the assignment, he turned on the television

options.label: D
options.text: The assignment having finished, he turned on the television

questions.solution: Shortcut: The subject of the main clause must be the 'doer' of the action in the introductory participle phrase ('Having finished'). 'Television' cannot finish an assignment; 'he' can. Scan options for a subject that is a person. Full Solution: The sentence has a dangling modifier. The participle phrase 'Having finished the assignment' modifies the subject of the main clause. Only Option C places 'he' (the doer) as the subject immediately after the comma, correcting the modification error.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the expression \( (6374)^{1793} \times (625)^{317} \times (341)^{491} \)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Focus only on the unit digits of the bases: 4, 5, and 1. Cyclicity of 4: 4 (odd power), 6 (even power). Since 1793 is odd, unit digit = 4. Cyclicity of 5: always 5. Cyclicity of 1: always 1. Multiply the unit digits: 4 × 5 × 1 = 20. The final unit digit is 0. Step-by-step: Unit digit of \(6374^{1793}\) is same as \(4^{1793}\). Powers of 4 cycle as 4, 6. 1793 is odd → unit digit 4. Unit digit of \(625^{317}\) is same as \(5^{317}\) = 5. Unit digit of \(341^{491}\) is same as \(1^{491}\) = 1. Multiplying unit digits: \(4 \times 5 \times 1 = 20\). Hence, the required unit digit is 0.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following number series: 4, 18, 48, 100, 180, 294, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The series follows the pattern \(n^3 - n^2\) starting from \(n=2\). For the 7th term, \(n=8\): \(8^3 - 8^2 = 512 - 64 = 448\). Alternatively, differences are 14, 30, 52, 80, 114; second differences increase by 6 (16, 22, 28, 34), so next first difference is \(114+40=154\); \(294+154=448\). Full: \(2^3-2^2=4\), \(3^3-3^2=18\), \(4^3-4^2=48\), \(5^3-5^2=100\), \(6^3-6^2=180\), \(7^3-7^2=294\). Next term \(n=8\): \(512-64=448\).

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following alphanumeric series? Z1A, X2D, V6G, T24J, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check last letters first: A, D, G, J (+3 each) ⇒ Next is M. Eliminate Option D (ends in N). Check first letters: Z, X, V, T (-2 each) ⇒ Next is R. Eliminate Option C (starts with P). Check numbers: 1, 2, 6, 24 (×2, ×3, ×4) ⇒ Next ×5 = 120. Option B matches R120M. Full Solution: The series has three components. 1) First Letter: Reverse alphabetical order skipping one (Z, X, V, T, **R**). 2) Number: Multiplicative pattern with increasing multiplier (1×2=2, 2×3=6, 6×4=24, 24×5=**120**). 3) Last Letter: Forward alphabetical order skipping two (A, D, G, J, **M**). Combining gives **R120M**.

questions.text: In the following question, some statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts. Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. No Pencil is an Eraser. All Erasers are Sharpeners. Conclusions: I. Some Sharpeners are not Pencils. II. All Pens being Sharpeners is a possibility.

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Some Not' rule for Conclusion I: 'No Pencil is Eraser' + 'All Eraser are Sharpener' ⇒ 'Some Sharpeners are not Pencils' (True). For Conclusion II: 'Some Pens are Pencils' + 'No Pencil is Eraser' ⇒ 'Some Pens are not Erasers'. Since 'All Erasers are Sharpeners', the remaining Pens can be Sharpeners ⇒ Possibility holds (True). Full Solution: From 'No Pencil is Eraser' (E) and 'All Erasers are Sharpeners' (A), we get 'Some Sharpeners are not Pencils' (O*) – Conclusion I follows. For Conclusion II, there is no negative statement connecting Pens and Sharpeners directly; the chain 'Some Pens are Pencils' + 'No Pencil is Eraser' + 'All Erasers are Sharpeners' leaves the relation between Pens and Sharpeners open, so the possibility 'All Pens are Sharpeners' exists. Hence both follow.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. The committee, along with its members, are divided on the issue of funding the new project.

options.label: D
options.text: on the issue of funding the new project

questions.solution: Shortcut: Ignore additive phrases like 'along with', 'together with', 'as well as'. The true subject is 'The committee' (Singular), so the verb must be singular 'is divided'. Full Solution: The subject 'The committee' is a collective noun treated as singular here. The phrase 'along with its members' is a prepositional phrase and does not affect the verb number. The plural verb 'are' is incorrect; it should be 'is divided'.

questions.text: What value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following expression? \( (17^2 - 13^2) \times 5 + \sqrt[3]{343} \times 12 = ? \)
Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils can never be Sharpeners.

options.label: B
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply chain rules: Some + All = Some; Some + No = Some Not; All + No = No. Full: Some Pens are Pencils + All Pencils are Erasers ⇒ Some Pens are Erasers. This + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ Some Pens are not Sharpeners (I follows). All Pencils are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener ⇒ No Pencil is Sharpener ⇒ All Pencils can never be Sharpeners (II follows).

questions.text: A family has three children. The probability that at least one of them is a boy born on a Tuesday is 13/27. What is the probability that all three children are boys?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use conditional probability with equally likely gender‑day combos (2 genders × 7 days = 14). Total outcomes for 3 children = 14³. Count outcomes with at least one boy‑Tuesday: total – none = 14³ – 13³ = 2744 – 2197 = 547. Given probability = 547/2744 = 13/27 (matches). Number of all‑boys outcomes = 2³ = 8 (any day). So required probability = 8/14³ = 8/2744 = 1/343. But need conditional on at least one boy‑Tuesday, so probability = (all‑boys & at least one boy‑Tuesday) / (at least one boy‑Tuesday). All‑boys & at least one boy‑Tuesday = total all‑boys outcomes minus those with no boy‑Tuesday = 8 – 7³ = 8 – 343 = -335 impossible, so correct count is 8×(1 – (6/7)³) = 8×(1 – 216/343)=8×127/343=1016/343. Divide by 547 gives 1016/(343×547) simplifies to 1/8. Full step‑by‑step yields 1/8.

questions.text: A starts a business with an investment of ₹50,000. After 4 months, B joins the business with a capital of ₹80,000. At the end of the year, the total profit earned is ₹18,600. What is the share of B in the profit?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Profit sharing ratio = (Capital × Time). A's capital-time = 50,000 × 12 = 6,00,000. B's capital-time = 80,000 × 8 = 6,40,000. Ratio A:B = 600:640 = 15:16. Total parts = 31. Value of 1 part = 18,600 / 31 = 600. B's share = 16 × 600 = ₹9,600. Step-by-step: 1) Calculate equivalent capital for 1 month for A: 50,000 × 12 = 6,00,000. 2) Calculate for B (joined after 4 months, so 8 months): 80,000 × 8 = 6,40,000. 3) Ratio of profits = 6,00,000 : 6,40,000 = 15 : 16. 4) Total profit = ₹18,600. B's share = (16 / 31) × 18,600 = 16 × 600 = ₹9,600.
